circ-basic.caption: Conventional current leaves the + terminal, flows round the loop and returns to the − terminal. The ammeter is in series, so the same current flows through it.

circ-meters.caption: A voltmeter is connected across the component (in parallel). An ammeter is placed in the path of the current (in series).

series-circuit.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 400 205" role="img" aria-label="Three resistors in series"><g transform="translate(50 70) rotate(90)"><line class="ln" x1="0" y1="0" x2="26" y2="0"/><line class="ln" x1="26" y1="-14" x2="26" y2="14"/><line class="ln" x1="34" y1="-7" x2="34" y2="7" style="stroke-width:5"/><line class="ln" x1="34" y1="0" x2="60" y2="0"/></g><line class="ln" x1="50" y1="70" x2="50" y2="40"/><line class="ln" x1="50" y1="40" x2="90" y2="40"/><g transform="translate(90 40) rotate(0)"><polyline class="ln" points="0,0 8,0 14,-9 23,9 32,-9 41,9 47,-9 52,0 60,0"/></g><text x="120" y="24" text-anchor="middle">R1</text><text x="120" y="66" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">V1</text><line class="ln" x1="150" y1="40" x2="170" y2="40"/><g transform="translate(170 40) rotate(0)"><polyline class="ln" points="0,0 8,0 14,-9 23,9 32,-9 41,9 47,-9 52,0 60,0"/></g><text x="200" y="24" text-anchor="middle">R2</text><text x="200" y="66" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">V2</text><line class="ln" x1="230" y1="40" x2="250" y2="40"/><g transform="translate(250 40) rotate(0)"><polyline class="ln" points="0,0 8,0 14,-9 23,9 32,-9 41,9 47,-9 52,0 60,0"/></g><text x="280" y="24" text-anchor="middle">R3</text><text x="280" y="66" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">V3</text><polyline class="ln" points="310,40 350,40 350,160 50,160 50,130"/><text x="36" y="96" text-anchor="end">+</text><text x="200" y="188" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">Same current I through every resistor</text></svg>
series-circuit.caption: Series: one path, the same current through every resistor. The voltages add up to the supply voltage, and the resistances add: R = R1 + R2 + R3.

parallel-circuit.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 400 225" role="img" aria-label="Two resistors in parallel"><g transform="translate(50 80) rotate(90)"><line class="ln" x1="0" y1="0" x2="26" y2="0"/><line class="ln" x1="26" y1="-14" x2="26" y2="14"/><line class="ln" x1="34" y1="-7" x2="34" y2="7" style="stroke-width:5"/><line class="ln" x1="34" y1="0" x2="60" y2="0"/></g><line class="ln" x1="50" y1="80" x2="50" y2="40"/><line class="ln" x1="50" y1="140" x2="50" y2="185"/><line class="ln" x1="50" y1="40" x2="250" y2="40"/><line class="ln" x1="50" y1="185" x2="250" y2="185"/><line class="ln" x1="150" y1="40" x2="150" y2="80"/><g transform="translate(150 80) rotate(90)"><polyline class="ln" points="0,0 8,0 14,-9 23,9 32,-9 41,9 47,-9 52,0 60,0"/></g><line class="ln" x1="150" y1="140" x2="150" y2="185"/><text x="172" y="114" text-anchor="start">R1</text><circle class="fl" cx="150" cy="40" r="3.5"/><circle class="fl" cx="150" cy="185" r="3.5"/><line class="ln" x1="250" y1="40" x2="250" y2="80"/><g transform="translate(250 80) rotate(90)"><polyline class="ln" points="0,0 8,0 14,-9 23,9 32,-9 41,9 47,-9 52,0 60,0"/></g><line class="ln" x1="250" y1="140" x2="250" y2="185"/><text x="272" y="114" text-anchor="start">R2</text><circle class="fl" cx="250" cy="40" r="3.5"/><circle class="fl" cx="250" cy="185" r="3.5"/><text x="36" y="114" text-anchor="end">+</text><text x="100" y="28" text-anchor="middle">I</text><text x="150" y="28" text-anchor="middle">I1</text><text x="250" y="28" text-anchor="middle">I2</text><text x="200" y="214" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">Same voltage across each branch</text></svg>
parallel-circuit.caption: Parallel: several paths, the same voltage across every branch. The branch currents add up: I = I1 + I2, and 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2.

kcl-junction.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 400 200" role="img" aria-label="Current flowing into and out of a junction"><line class="ln" x1="60" y1="45" x2="200" y2="100"/><line class="ln" x1="60" y1="155" x2="200" y2="100"/><line class="ln" x1="200" y1="100" x2="340" y2="100"/><circle class="fl" cx="200" cy="100" r="5"/><polygon class="fl2" points="0,0 -10,-4.5 -10,4.5" transform="translate(137.0 75.25) rotate(21.44773632710535)"/><polygon class="fl2" points="0,0 -10,-4.5 -10,4.5" transform="translate(137.0 124.75) rotate(-21.44773632710535)"/><polygon class="fl2" points="0,0 -10,-4.5 -10,4.5" transform="translate(284.0 100.0) rotate(0.0)"/><text x="60" y="36" text-anchor="start">I1 = 3 A (in)</text><text x="60" y="180" text-anchor="start">I2 = 2 A (in)</text><text x="340" y="88" text-anchor="end">I3 = 5 A (out)</text><text x="200" y="196" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">Junction: current in = current out</text></svg>
kcl-junction.caption: Kirchhoff's current law: the current into a junction equals the current out of it, so 3 A + 2 A = 5 A.

kvl-loop.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 400 205" role="img" aria-label="Series loop with voltage drops"><g transform="translate(50 70) rotate(90)"><line class="ln" x1="0" y1="0" x2="26" y2="0"/><line class="ln" x1="26" y1="-14" x2="26" y2="14"/><line class="ln" x1="34" y1="-7" x2="34" y2="7" style="stroke-width:5"/><line class="ln" x1="34" y1="0" x2="60" y2="0"/></g><line class="ln" x1="50" y1="70" x2="50" y2="40"/><line class="ln" x1="50" y1="40" x2="100" y2="40"/><g transform="translate(100 40) rotate(0)"><polyline class="ln" points="0,0 8,0 14,-9 23,9 32,-9 41,9 47,-9 52,0 60,0"/></g><text x="130" y="24" text-anchor="middle">R1 = 2 Ω</text><text x="130" y="66" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">V1 = 4 V</text><line class="ln" x1="160" y1="40" x2="220" y2="40"/><g transform="translate(220 40) rotate(0)"><polyline class="ln" points="0,0 8,0 14,-9 23,9 32,-9 41,9 47,-9 52,0 60,0"/></g><text x="250" y="24" text-anchor="middle">R2 = 4 Ω</text><text x="250" y="66" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">V2 = 8 V</text><polyline class="ln" points="280,40 350,40 350,160 50,160 50,130"/><text x="36" y="96" text-anchor="end">+</text><text x="36" y="118" text-anchor="end">12 V</text><text x="200" y="188" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">KVL: 12 − 4 − 8 = 0, with I = 12 / 6 = 2 A</text></svg>
kvl-loop.caption: Kirchhoff's voltage law: going round the loop, the source voltage equals the sum of the drops: 12 V = 4 V + 8 V.

rlc-series.caption: A series RLC circuit: the same current flows through all three. Z = √(R² + (XL − XC)²).

imp-triangle.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 440 208" role="img" aria-label="Impedance triangle"><polyline class="ln" points="60,160 300,160 300,50 60,160"/><text x="180" y="182" text-anchor="middle">R</text><text x="312" y="112" text-anchor="start">X = XL − XC</text><text x="150" y="92" text-anchor="end">Z</text><text x="100" y="152" text-anchor="start">φ</text><rect x="288" y="148" width="12" height="12" class="ln"/><text x="220" y="203" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">Z² = R² + X²,  cosφ = R / Z (power factor)</text></svg>
imp-triangle.caption: The impedance triangle: resistance R and net reactance X are at right angles, and Z is the hypotenuse. The angle φ is the phase angle.

power-triangle.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 440 208" role="img" aria-label="Power triangle"><polyline class="ln" points="60,160 300,160 300,50 60,160"/><text x="180" y="182" text-anchor="middle">P (kW)</text><text x="312" y="112" text-anchor="start">Q (kvar)</text><text x="150" y="92" text-anchor="end">S (kVA)</text><text x="100" y="152" text-anchor="start">φ</text><rect x="288" y="148" width="12" height="12" class="ln"/><text x="220" y="203" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">S² = P² + Q²,  P = S cosφ,  Q = S sinφ</text></svg>
power-triangle.caption: The power triangle: active power P and reactive power Q are at right angles, and apparent power S is the hypotenuse. cosφ is the power factor.

three-phase-wave.caption: The three phase voltages R, Y and B have the same size and are 120° apart. Together they deliver smooth, nearly constant power.

star-connection.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 420 262" role="img" aria-label="Star (wye) connection"><line class="ln" x1="130" y1="135" x2="130.0" y2="115.0"/><g transform="translate(130.0 115.0) rotate(-90)"><polyline class="ln" points="0,0 8,0 14,-9 23,9 32,-9 41,9 47,-9 52,0 60,0"/></g><line class="ln" x1="130.0" y1="55.0" x2="130.0" y2="25.0"/><circle class="ln" cx="130.0" cy="25.0" r="4" style="fill:var(--panel)"/><text x="130.0" y="15.0" text-anchor="middle">R</text><line class="ln" x1="130" y1="135" x2="112.67949192431122" y2="145.0"/><g transform="translate(112.67949192431122 145.0) rotate(150)"><polyline class="ln" points="0,0 8,0 14,-9 23,9 32,-9 41,9 47,-9 52,0 60,0"/></g><line class="ln" x1="60.7179676972449" y1="175.0" x2="34.73720558371174" y2="190.0"/><circle class="ln" cx="34.73720558371174" cy="190.0" r="4" style="fill:var(--panel)"/><text x="20.73720558371174" y="206.0" text-anchor="middle">Y</text><line class="ln" x1="130" y1="135" x2="147.32050807568876" y2="145.0"/><g transform="translate(147.32050807568876 145.0) rotate(30)"><polyline class="ln" points="0,0 8,0 14,-9 23,9 32,-9 41,9 47,-9 52,0 60,0"/></g><line class="ln" x1="199.2820323027551" y1="175.0" x2="225.26279441628827" y2="190.0"/><circle class="ln" cx="225.26279441628827" cy="190.0" r="4" style="fill:var(--panel)"/><text x="239.26279441628827" y="206.0" text-anchor="middle">B</text><circle class="fl" cx="130" cy="135" r="5"/><text x="140" y="129" text-anchor="start">N</text><text x="260" y="100" text-anchor="start">VL = √3 × Vph</text><text x="260" y="125" text-anchor="start">IL = Iph</text><text x="260" y="150" text-anchor="start" class="mu">N = neutral point</text></svg>
star-connection.caption: Star connection: three impedances meet at the neutral point N. The line voltage is √3 times the phase voltage, and the line current equals the phase current.

delta-connection.caption: Delta connection: three impedances form a closed triangle. The line voltage equals the phase voltage, and the line current is √3 times the phase current.

ct-vt-connection.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 440 255" role="img" aria-label="CT and VT connected to a relay"><line class="ln" x1="20" y1="50" x2="420" y2="50"/><circle class="ln" cx="110" cy="50" r="13"/><line class="ln" x1="102" y1="61" x2="102" y2="170"/><line class="ln" x1="118" y1="61" x2="118" y2="170"/><text x="110" y="26" text-anchor="middle">CT 400/5 A</text><polygon class="fl2" points="0,0 -10,-4.5 -10,4.5" transform="translate(60 50) rotate(0)"/><text x="60" y="40" text-anchor="middle">I</text><circle class="fl" cx="300" cy="50" r="3.5"/><line class="ln" x1="300" y1="50" x2="300" y2="76"/><circle class="ln" cx="300" cy="90" r="14"/><circle class="ln" cx="300" cy="110" r="14"/><line class="ln" x1="300" y1="124" x2="300" y2="170"/><text x="322" y="100" text-anchor="start">VT 11000/110 V</text><rect class="ln" x="80" y="170" width="280" height="36"/><text x="220" y="193" text-anchor="middle">Relay / meter</text><text x="220" y="232" text-anchor="middle" class="mu">Never open a CT secondary. ct-vt-connection.caption: A CT is connected in series with the line and gives a small current. A VT is connected across the line and gives a small voltage. Both feed relays and meters.
